claims.text: The rider did precisely what POL-NS-04(a) requires. At 18:10:20, inside the waiting window (arrival 18:10:00, termination 18:14:00), the rider sent the only message on this trip: 'I am by the pickup pin and cannot see you. Where are you?' That single message is both a statement that the rider cannot see the vehicle and a request for the driver's position, which is limb (a) on its plain words. The message was delivered at 18:10:21 and read at 18:10:22.

POL-NS-04(b) is satisfied on the platform's own records, not on the rider's say-so. The chat log contains exactly one message and it is the rider's; there is no driver reply anywhere in it. The trip record's in_app_calls array is empty, so no in-app voice call was placed at any point before the driver terminated the trip at 18:14:00. The driver therefore neither answered in the chat within 120 seconds of the rider's message nor called.

The interval of silence is 218 seconds - from the driver's read receipt at 18:10:22 to the termination at 18:14:00 - which is longer than the 120-second reply window POL-NS-04(b) allows, and in any event the driver never replied at all. This is not a rider who went dark on a driver who was trying to coordinate: it is a driver who read the rider's locating message and terminated the trip without a word.

Limb (c) of POL-NS-04 cannot be run on this record, and it must not be treated as if it had been failed. The source trace carries no rider track at all (the rider_presence block reports available: false), so limb (c) is undecidable and neutral: it is neither satisfied nor failed, and neither advocate nor the Judge may infer from its absence that the rider was elsewhere. POL-NS-11 is explicit that the absent rider track is not evidence for any deciding fact of the remaining clauses, does not impair the driver's arrival or dwell evidence, does not by itself engage POL-NS-08(b) or POL-NS-09(e), and does not lower the confidence cap on a finding that rests on the driver's own track.

I do not put limb (c) higher than the record supports, and I do not ask the Judge to stretch it. Because there are no rider fixes in the trace, the rider cannot affirmatively satisfy limb (c), and POL-NS-11 states that POL-NS-04 therefore cannot by itself exonerate the rider. The rider's presence at the pin rests on the rider's own contemporaneous chat message of 18:10:20, and no artifact in this bundle contradicts it; that is the whole of the rider's case on presence, and I state it no higher than that.

I do not allege a false arrival marker, because the rider's own trace does not permit it and I will not overstate the point. The driver's first fix is at 18:10:00, the identical timestamp to the 'arrived' event, at a minimum, mean and maximum distance of 0 m from the pickup pin and a recorded speed of 0 kph. POL-NS-05 is therefore not available to the rider on this record, and I do not press it.

No traffic advisory covers this pickup road. EV-ADVIS-00853-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and fires the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT; I disclose that impairment as POL-GEN-02(1) requires. Its absence is nonetheless citable, and under POL-NS-06 a MISSING traffic_advisory makes limb (i) unavailable, so the driver cannot invoke a kerbside restriction, enforcement, closure or accident to accumulate or extend the required waiting period on this trip.

claims.text: All four limbs of the baseline chargeable no-show are carried on this record. Limb (a): the trip record contains a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-09-13T18:10:00+08:00. Limb (b): the driver's own trace places him at the pickup pin (maximum distance from the pin 0.0 m, mean 0.0 m) at that same timestamp, i.e. inside the arrival geofence before or at the arrival event. The first qualifying in-geofence fix and the arrival tap coincide, so the waiting clock starts at 18:10:00 on any reading.

Limb (c) is satisfied on the arithmetic. The GPS trace carries 25 consecutive qualifying in-geofence fixes in a single uninterrupted run from 18:10:00 to 18:14:00, i.e. a continuous dwell of 240 seconds. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), and no_show_threshold_sec is null, so no longer threshold applies. 240 seconds is 60 seconds clear of the required minimum, and the legacy minimum_dwell_sec table figure for TRANSPORT_HUB is not in play because resolution_rule confines it to records authored before policy version 2 and never applies it to a record that carries platform_policy.

The required dwell of 180 seconds elapsed at 18:13:00, and the trip was terminated by the driver one minute later at 18:14:00 - at or after that moment. Limb (d) is therefore satisfied: the record shows no boarding event and a driver-terminated trip with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes the limb recognises. The rider's own message ('I am by the pickup pin and cannot see you') confirms to the driver that the rider was not at the vehicle, and no boarding event anywhere in the trip record contradicts the termination code.

The POL-NS-02 proximity test is met with room to spare. That test requires at least 3 consecutive qualifying fixes inside the arrival radius; this trace yields 25 qualifying fixes, all of them inside. The applicable radius is the TRANSPORT_HUB radius of 150 m, and the zone class is taken from trip_record (pickup_zone_class TRANSPORT_HUB, pickup at Tampines MRT, a registered interchange private-hire bay), not assumed to be STANDARD. The driver's distance from the pin never exceeded 0.0 m, so even the STANDARD 50 m radius would be satisfied several times over.

POL-NS-05 does not bite, and the driver does not need its escape hatch. It is triggered only by an arrival marker more than 300 m from the pin or a driver moving at 15 km/h or more at the marker timestamp. At 18:10:00 the driver was 0.0 m from the pin and his only recorded speed across the whole stationary window is 0 kph, so the arrival marker is TRUE and the waiting clock runs from the arrival event itself. No false-marker referral arises.

POL-NS-03 is not available on these facts. That clause governs a driver stationary outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin. The driver's fixes are not outside the radius at all - they are at 0.0 m from the pin - so there is no wrong-entrance mislocation to allocate and no route to the full refund this clause would otherwise license.

The rider's contact-based exoneration under POL-NS-04 fails at limb (c), and the clause therefore does not apply at all. I do not dispute limbs (a) and (b): the rider's single message at 18:10:20 is locating in content, and the trip record records no driver chat reply and in_app_calls is empty. But limb (c) requires the rider's own track to place the rider's device within 200 m of the pin for the majority of qualifying fixes across the waiting window, and the trace carries no rider track at all (derived.rider_presence.available is false). Under POL-NS-11 that makes limb (c) undecidable rather than satisfied, the clause cannot exonerate the rider, and the dispute is decided on the driver's own evidence under POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-07.

The absent rider track must not be allowed to drag this case to human review. POL-NS-11 states expressly that a missing rider_track is not the evidence for any deciding fact of the arrival and dwell clauses, does not impair the gps_trace for the driver's arrival or dwell, does not by itself engage POL-NS-08(b) or POL-NS-09(e), and does not lower the confidence cap on a finding that rests on the driver's track. The deciding facts here - arrival position and dwell duration - rest on the driver's own trace and the trip record, both of which are COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The arrival and dwell evidence is methodologically clean, so no POL-NS-08 defect defeats the fee. Limbs (a) to (d) are all absent: the arrival event timestamp matches the nearest GPS fix exactly (zero skew, well inside the 90 second limit); the trace carries 25 fixes at a 10 second cadence with no gap longer than 10 seconds, far more than the 6-fix minimum and with no gap over 120 seconds inside the waiting window; the chat log holds 1 message, equal to trip_record.chat_message_count of 1, with no msg_id gap and no content redaction; and the fare line of 4.50 SGD reconciles with the net figure produced by resolution_rule (platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd 4.50).

Disclosure on the one impaired artifact in the bundle: EV-ADVIS-00853-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY) is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. The driver relies on it for nothing. POL-NS-06 limb (i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where such an advisory is present and populated; here the dwell was a single continuous in-geofence run of 240 seconds, so no accumulation across intervals is required and limb (i) is simply not engaged. The absence of an advisory therefore does not shorten, extend or excuse anything, and its weight of 0.0 does not cap confidence in a finding that rests on the trip record and the driver's trace instead.

POL-NS-06 licenses no refund here. It refunds only where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period in force. Measured under POL-NS-02 and uncorrected because POL-NS-05 finds no false marker, the dwell is 240 seconds against a 180 second minimum - a surplus, not a shortfall. The rider was charged the cancellation fee and nothing else: the fare breakdown carries a cancellation line of 4.50 SGD and a waiting-time line of 0.00 SGD, and POL-NS-10(d) forbids both a cancellation fee and a waiting-time fee on one trip, so the 4.50 is the only contested amount.

The driver's compensation is payable and is not caught by the anti-farming check. POL-NS-07 pays 80 percent of the cancellation fee in force - 80 percent of 4.50 SGD, i.e. 3.60 SGD - which is exactly the driver_compensation figure the fare breakdown computes. The withholding test requires BOTH limbs: no_show_terminations_30d of 4 or more, AND that count divided by completed_trips_30d greater than 0.08. The driver profile shows no_show_terminations_30d of 1 and completed_trips_30d of 100, so the first limb fails (1 is below 4) and the ratio is 0.01, nowhere near 0.08. Compensation is paid and no POL-NS-09(d) escalation follows.

No escalation trigger is present on this record. There is no contradiction between artifacts on arrival, dwell or rider presence - the trip record's arrival event and the GPS trace agree to the second and both place the driver at the pin throughout. Neither profile shows a counterparty dispute pattern: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so POL-NS-09(c) is not reached, and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, so POL-NS-09(d) is not reached. The lifetime counters on the profiles (prior_no_show_flags) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and are not the fields these limbs read. The case is decidable without human review.

On the outcome: the rider filed this dispute, the charge still stands (fare_breakdown.payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), and the fee was validly earned, so the rider's claim is not supported and the present state stands as to the fee. The ruling the case produces is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd mirroring driver_compensation_sgd at 3.60 SGD, because under POL-GEN-03 that value is the amount the ruling moves and the driver is the party owed money; the rider's own charge is left standing.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this is a no-show cancellation-fee dispute on trip TRP-00853. The rider filed it, contesting the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee. On the evidence, the fee stands and the driver is entitled to compensation.

Why the fee stands. The driver pressed 'arrived' at 18:10:00 at the Tampines MRT pickup, which the trip record classes as a TRANSPORT_HUB (arrival radius 150 m). The GPS trace EV-GPS-00853 places him at the pin itself — maximum, mean and minimum distance 0.0 m — stationary at 0 kph from 18:10:00 to 18:14:00, a single continuous in-geofence dwell of 240 seconds. The free waiting period in force is 180 seconds (EV-TRIP-00853, platform_policy.free_wait_sec), and no_show_threshold_sec is null. All four limbs of POL-NS-01 therefore hold: (a) the trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event; (b) the trace places the driver inside the geofence at that timestamp; (c) he held position for 240 seconds against a 180-second minimum, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix; and (d) the driver terminated the trip at 18:14:00 — after the dwell elapsed at 18:13:00 — with no boarding event and the recognised reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. The arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05 (he was 0 m from the pin at 0 kph, nowhere near 300 m or 15 kph). POL-NS-03, the wrong-entrance clause, does not apply because the driver was inside the arrival radius, not merely within 400 m of it. POL-NS-06 gives no refund because the dwell was a surplus, not a shortfall, against the minimum.

The rider's message. At 18:10:20 the rider sent the only message on the trip: 'I am by the pickup pin and cannot see you. Where are you?' That is a locating and coordinating message, and the driver neither replied within 120 seconds nor placed any in-app call (in_app_calls is empty), so POL-NS-04 limbs (a) and (b) hold. But limb (c) cannot be run: the trace carries no rider track at all (derived.rider_presence.available is false). Under POL-NS-11 the limb is UNDECIDABLE — neither satisfied nor failed — so POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider, and the fee is decided on the driver's own evidence. I have not inferred from the silence of the rider track that the rider was elsewhere, and per POL-NS-11 that missing track does not impair the driver's arrival or dwell evidence, does not engage POL-NS-08(b) or POL-NS-09(e), and does not lower the confidence cap on a finding resting on the driver's track.

Impaired artifact. The only impaired artifact is EV-ADVIS-00853-01 (traffic advisory), MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT. Nobody relies on it: it could only bear on POL-NS-06 limb (i), which permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where a populated advisory exists — and here the dwell was one continuous 240-second run, so limb (i) is not engaged. Its absence is citable but shortens, extends and excuses nothing.

Money and outcome. Under POL-NS-07 the driver is paid 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee = SGD 3.60, the exact figure the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00853) computes. To both parties: this dispute concerns the SGD 4.50 no-show cancellation fee on trip TRP-00853 (EV-FARE-00853: cancellation_fee 4.50, total_charged 4.50, payment_status CHARGED). The rider asks for it back; it stands.

THE CHARGE IS VALID UNDER POL-NS-01. All four limbs hold on this record. (a) The trip record (EV-TRIP-00853) contains a driver 'arrived' event at 18:10:00. (b) The GPS trace (EV-GPS-00853) places the driver 0.0 m from the pickup pin at that same timestamp, well inside the TRANSPORT_HUB arrival radius of 150 m (POL-NS-02), and POL-NS-02's consecutive-fix test is met 25 times over. (c) The driver held position at 0.0 m for a single continuous in-geofence run of 240 seconds, from 18:10:00 to 18:14:00, against the free waiting period of 180 seconds in force for this trip (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec); no longer threshold applies because no_show_threshold_sec is null. (d) The trip record records no boarding event and a driver termination at 18:14:00 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one minute after the required dwell elapsed at 18:13:00.

POL-NS-05 does not bite and produces no referral: at 18:10:00 the driver was stationary at the pin at a recorded 0 kph, so the arrival marker is TRUE and the waiting clock runs from the arrival event itself.

THE RIDER'S CONTACT DOES NOT EXONERATE. The rider's message at 18:10:20 ('I am by the pickup pin and cannot see you. Where are you?') satisfies POL-NS-04 limbs (a) and (b): it is locating in content, and the driver neither replied in the chat within 120 seconds nor placed any in-app call before terminating. But limb (c) requires the rider's own track to place the rider's device within 200 m of the pin for the majority of qualifying fixes, and the trace carries no rider track at all (rider_presence.available is false). Under POL-NS-11 that makes limb (c) UNDECIDABLE, not failed: POL-NS-04 cannot by itself exonerate the rider, and the missing rider track does not impair the driver's arrival or dwell evidence, does not engage POL-NS-08(b) or POL-NS-09(e), and does not lower the confidence cap on a finding that rests on the driver's track. The dispute is therefore decided on the driver's evidence under POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-07. I record both advocates' agreement on this point.

WEIGHT AND INTEGRITY. The artifacts carrying the deciding facts are EV-TRIP-00853 and EV-GPS-00853, both at weight 1.0. The arrival event timestamp matches the nearest GPS fix exactly (no clock skew), the trace holds 25 fixes at a 10-second cadence with no gap over 120 seconds and no gap straddling the cancellation, the chat log's 1 message equals trip_record.chat_message_count of 1 with no redaction, and the 4.50 charged reconciles with the net figure produced by the resolution rule. The single impaired artifact, EV-ADVIS-00853-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT), carries no deciding fact here, because the dwell was one continuous run and no accumulation under POL-NS-06(i) was needed; it therefore does not cap confidence and its absence is not relied on by the driver. No POL-NS-03 mislocation arises (the driver was inside the radius, at the pin).

OUTCOME. The rider's claim to have the charge returned is not supported, and the charge stands as it presently is. Under POL-NS-07 the driver is compensated at 80 percent of the 4.50 fee = 3.60 SGD, the figure the fare breakdown itself computes. The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (below the 4 threshold) and the ratio to 100 completed trips in 30 days is 0.01 (below 0.08). No POL-NS-09 escalation trigger is present: confidence is above the 0.70 floor, the artifacts do not contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence, neither profile shows counterparty disputes in the last 90 days (both 0), rider no-show disputes in 30 days is 0, and the sole impaired artifact is not the evidence for any deciding fact. The profile fields cited (no_show_terminations_30d, completed_trips_30d) are the ones POL-NS-07 names; the lifetime counters are treated as context only, per POL-GEN-01. The ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and per POL-GEN-03 amount_sgd carries the same 3.60 figure because that is the amount the ruling moves; the rider's own charge stands. The monetary effect (3.60) does not exceed the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of 8.00, so it executes automatically on issue, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

The anti-farming check does not trip: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1 (below 4) and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 100 is 0.01 (not above 0.08). Compensation is paid, so per POL-GEN-03 the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION and amount_sgd mirrors driver_compensation_sgd at SGD 3.60 — it is the amount the ruling moves, not a refund to the rider; the rider's SGD 4.50 charge stands.

NO ESCALATION. There is no contradiction between admissible artifacts on arrival, dwell or rider presence; rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0 and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0; the anti-farming check does not trip; and the deciding facts rest on EV-GPS-00853 and EV-TRIP-00853, both COMPLETE at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0 and confidence is stated at 0.90, above the 0.70 floor. The lifetime counters mentioned on the profiles (prior_no_show_flags) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and were not used.

NO REFERRALS. No clause produces one: POL-NS-05(ii) does not fire because the arrival marker is true, the POL-NS-07 anti-farming branch does not trip, the reason code recorded (RIDER_NO_SHOW) is a recognised one rather than a mis-selected code, and no RD clause is engaged. The monetary effect, SGD 3.60, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold (POL-GEN-05), so this provisional ruling executes automatically; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), and no_show_threshold_sec is null, so no longer threshold applies. 240 seconds is 60 seconds clear of the required minimum, and the legacy minimum_dwell_sec table figure for TRANSPORT_HUB is not in play because resolution_rule confines it to records authored before policy version 2 and never applies it to a record that carries platform_policy.

The required dwell of 180 seconds elapsed at 18:13:00, and the trip was terminated by the driver one minute later at 18:14:00 - at or after that moment. Limb (d) is therefore satisfied: the record shows no boarding event and a driver-terminated trip with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes the limb recognises. The rider's own message ('I am by the pickup pin and cannot see you') confirms to the driver that the rider was not at the vehicle, and no boarding event anywhere in the trip record contradicts the termination code.

The POL-NS-02 proximity test is met with room to spare. That test requires at least 3 consecutive qualifying fixes inside the arrival radius; this trace yields 25 qualifying fixes, all of them inside. The applicable radius is the TRANSPORT_HUB radius of 150 m, and the zone class is taken from trip_record (pickup_zone_class TRANSPORT_HUB, pickup at Tampines MRT, a registered interchange private-hire bay), not assumed to be STANDARD. The driver's distance from the pin never exceeded 0.0 m, so even the STANDARD 50 m radius would be satisfied several times over.

POL-NS-05 does not bite, and the driver does not need its escape hatch. It is triggered only by an arrival marker more than 300 m from the pin or a driver moving at 15 km/h or more at the marker timestamp. At 18:10:00 the driver was 0.0 m from the pin and his only recorded speed across the whole stationary window is 0 kph, so the arrival marker is TRUE and the waiting clock runs from the arrival event itself. No false-marker referral arises.

POL-NS-03 is not available on these facts. That clause governs a driver stationary outside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin. The driver's fixes are not outside the radius at all - they are at 0.0 m from the pin - so there is no wrong-entrance mislocation to allocate and no route to the full refund this clause would otherwise license.

The rider's contact-based exoneration under POL-NS-04 fails at limb (c), and the clause therefore does not apply at all. I do not dispute limbs (a) and (b): the rider's single message at 18:10:20 is locating in content, and the trip record records no driver chat reply and in_app_calls is empty. But limb (c) requires the rider's own track to place the rider's device within 200 m of the pin for the majority of qualifying fixes across the waiting window, and the trace carries no rider track at all (derived.rider_presence.available is false). Under POL-NS-11 that makes limb (c) undecidable rather than satisfied, the clause cannot exonerate the rider, and the dispute is decided on the driver's own evidence under POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-07.

The absent rider track must not be allowed to drag this case to human review. POL-NS-11 states expressly that a missing rider_track is not the evidence for any deciding fact of the arrival and dwell clauses, does not impair the gps_trace for the driver's arrival or dwell, does not by itself engage POL-NS-08(b) or POL-NS-09(e), and does not lower the confidence cap on a finding that rests on the driver's track. The deciding facts here - arrival position and dwell duration - rest on the driver's own trace and the trip record, both of which are COMPLETE at weight 1.0.

The arrival and dwell evidence is methodologically clean, so no POL-NS-08 defect defeats the fee. Limbs (a) to (d) are all absent: the arrival event timestamp matches the nearest GPS fix exactly (zero skew, well inside the 90 second limit); the trace carries 25 fixes at a 10 second cadence with no gap longer than 10 seconds, far more than the 6-fix minimum and with no gap over 120 seconds inside the waiting window; the chat log holds 1 message, equal to trip_record.chat_message_count of 1, with no msg_id gap and no content redaction; and the fare line of 4.50 SGD reconciles with the net figure produced by resolution_rule (platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd 4.50).

Disclosure on the one impaired artifact in the bundle: EV-ADVIS-00853-01 (TRAFFIC_ADVISORY) is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and fired the issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT. The driver relies on it for nothing. POL-NS-06 limb (i) permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed only where such an advisory is present and populated; here the dwell was a single continuous in-geofence run of 240 seconds, so no accumulation across intervals is required and limb (i) is simply not engaged. The absence of an advisory therefore does not shorten, extend or excuse anything, and its weight of 0.0 does not cap confidence in a finding that rests on the trip record and the driver's trace instead.

POL-NS-06 licenses no refund here. It refunds only where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period in force. Measured under POL-NS-02 and uncorrected because POL-NS-05 finds no false marker, the dwell is 240 seconds against a 180 second minimum - a surplus, not a shortfall. The rider was charged the cancellation fee and nothing else: the fare breakdown carries a cancellation line of 4.50 SGD and a waiting-time line of 0.00 SGD, and POL-NS-10(d) forbids both a cancellation fee and a waiting-time fee on one trip, so the 4.50 is the only contested amount.

The driver's compensation is payable and is not caught by the anti-farming check. POL-NS-07 pays 80 percent of the cancellation fee in force - 80 percent of 4.50 SGD, i.e. 3.60 SGD - which is exactly the driver_compensation figure the fare breakdown computes. The withholding test requires BOTH limbs: no_show_terminations_30d of 4 or more, AND that count divided by completed_trips_30d greater than 0.08. The driver profile shows no_show_terminations_30d of 1 and completed_trips_30d of 100, so the first limb fails (1 is below 4) and the ratio is 0.01, nowhere near 0.08. Compensation is paid and no POL-NS-09(d) escalation follows.

No escalation trigger is present on this record. There is no contradiction between artifacts on arrival, dwell or rider presence - the trip record's arrival event and the GPS trace agree to the second and both place the driver at the pin throughout. Neither profile shows a counterparty dispute pattern: rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so POL-NS-09(c) is not reached, and rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, so POL-NS-09(d) is not reached. The lifetime counters on the profiles (prior_no_show_flags) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and are not the fields these limbs read. The case is decidable without human review.

On the outcome: the rider filed this dispute, the charge still stands (fare_breakdown.payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), and the fee was validly earned, so the rider's claim is not supported and the present state stands as to the fee. The ruling the case produces is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd mirroring driver_compensation_sgd at 3.60 SGD, because under POL-GEN-03 that value is the amount the ruling moves and the driver is the party owed money; the rider's own charge is left standing.
